general_query_list.answer: Kickoff of FleetCare, a maintenance scheduling platform for the company's truck depots. Operations described missed services and 41 unplanned breakdowns last quarter. The team agreed to host on AWS (already vendor-assessed), to use PostgreSQL as the primary database for the scheduling service, to pilot at the Pune depot with go-live on 15 January, and to build the mechanics' app for Android only in the first release since all company phones are Android. Tom's idea of SMS alerts was parked pending input from depot leads.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Okay, I think everyone's here. Let's get started, thanks for making time. So this is the kickoff for FleetCare, the maintenance scheduling platform.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Morning.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Quick round of intros for Sara since she's new to the group?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Sara
meeting_transcripts.content: Yeah, hi, I'm Sara, I handle security and compliance. Mostly the audits and vendor reviews.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Arjun, engineering lead. I'll own the build.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: Meera, data and analytics. I'll be doing the reporting side and, later, the breakdown predictions.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: And Tom, operations. Basically I'm the one whose mechanics are going to use this thing every day, so, no pressure.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Right. So the problem. Tom, do you want to describe it?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Sure. Right now maintenance is scheduled on a shared spreadsheet per depot. Trucks miss services, parts aren't ordered on time, and when a truck breaks down on the highway we lose two, three days. Last quarter we had forty-one unplanned breakdowns across the four depots.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: And about a third of those were trucks that were already overdue for service according to the spreadsheet. So the data was there, nobody acted on it.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Okay. So today I want to settle the foundational things so Arjun's team can start. Hosting, database, the pilot plan, and what the mechanics' app looks like. Let's start with hosting.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: So two options really. We run it in our own server room at head office, or we go to the cloud. My strong preference is cloud. The server room is already at capacity and we don't have anyone on call at weekends.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Sara
meeting_transcripts.content: From my side cloud is fine as long as it's a provider we've already done a vendor assessment on. We did AWS last year for the billing system. Azure we haven't reviewed.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Does cloud mean it goes down when the depot internet goes down?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: The server side won't, but the depot would lose access, yes. We'll come back to that with the app design.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Cost-wise?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: For the pilot it's small. I estimated around eight hundred dollars a month.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Okay. Any objections to AWS?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: None from me. The billing data is already there, so joining to it later is easier.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Then let's lock it: FleetCare will be hosted on AWS. Sara, you don't need a new vendor review.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Sara
meeting_transcripts.content: Correct, the existing assessment covers it.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Good. Database.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: For the scheduling service I want PostgreSQL. Work orders, trucks, parts, schedules, it's all very relational. And the team knows it well.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: Works for me. I'd want read access for reporting, maybe a replica later.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: I don't have an opinion on databases, I'll be honest.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Ha, fair. Arjun, is anybody arguing for something else?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Someone on my team floated MongoDB, but I don't see the reason for it here.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Okay, so PostgreSQL is the primary database for the scheduling service. Agreed?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Agreed.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: Yes.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Next, the pilot. Tom, which depot?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Pune. It's our biggest depot, sixty-two trucks, and the depot manager there actually wants this. Nagpur would fight us.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Pune also has the best network connection of the four, which helps.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Timeline? I'd like something running before the financial year planning.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: If we start next week, a usable pilot by mid January is realistic. Not polished, but usable.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Mid January is good for us. December is peak season and I don't want to change anything in December.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: So the pilot goes live at the Pune depot on the fifteenth of January. Let's write that down as the target.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Yes. Fifteenth of Jan, Pune.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: Will we have historical data loaded by then? I'd want at least a year of service history in it.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: We can import the spreadsheets, yes. Cleaning them is another matter.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: I'll help with that.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Okay, the mechanics' app.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: The mechanics will use it on phones in the workshop. They need to see today's jobs, mark them done, log the parts used. Big buttons. Some of them wear gloves.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Question is Android, iOS, or both. Both roughly doubles the testing.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Every mechanic phone we issue is Android. The company bought Samsung handsets for all depots two years ago.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Then I'd say Android only for the first release. We can revisit iOS if it ever matters.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Sara
meeting_transcripts.content: Company-issued devices also make device management easier for me, we already have MDM on those.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Android-only for release one, then. Everyone okay?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Yep.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: Fine.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: One more idea. Maybe we send SMS alerts to the mechanics when a job is assigned? Some of them don't check apps.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: SMS costs money per message and we'd need a gateway. Not sure.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Sara
meeting_transcripts.content: And phone numbers are personal data, I'd want to look at that.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Let's park SMS. It's a good idea but we haven't got enough to decide. Tom, can you find out how many mechanics would actually want it?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: I can ask the depot leads.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Okay. Actions. Arjun, set up the AWS account and the repo this week. Meera, start pulling the spreadsheets together. Tom, the SMS question. Sara, can you send Arjun the AWS assessment document?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Sara
meeting_transcripts.content: Will do, today.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Sounds good.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Great. Same time in two weeks. Thanks all.
